title: @GlobalScope method hides local method but tooltip hints otherwise
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 
  - 4.4.1.stable
  - 4.5.dev [99f5a3d]

### System information

Godot v4.1.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop - Intel i7-12700H (20 threads)

### Issue description

Related to: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106944

Note: Split off the "adding new warnings" part to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14425, since that was not the original issue.

If a script uses the same method name as a `@GlobalScope` method, the latter is called. However, the editor hints at the local function instead of the `@GlobalScope` function. 

It is also weird that the local method does not override the `@GlobalScope` method, but it can exist without warnings.

I think the local method should hide the global method and print a warning, so that any new `@GlobalScope` method would not break compatibility if a name collision occurs, while also not encouraging method hiding. 
e.g. godotengine/godot-proposals#6652

Notes:
- happens regardless of being an `Autoload` or not
-  happens regardless of having `class_name` or not

Screenshots:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/664b6d16-a8e9-4a8f-be97-1d15318d8817)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d38f9da-29f9-44d7-a6c1-4022c6235f4b)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project and run it in the editor
2. Hover the cursor over the `log()` method call

(probably not project-dependent)
